title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Sensor / SpO₂ Reading Errors
description: Guide for troubleshooting inaccurate SpO₂ readings and sensor errors on the Masimo Rad-97 pulse oximeter, emphasizing external causes first.

steps.title: Check Sensor Connection
steps.instructions: Verify the sensor is fully seated in the oximeter port. Inspect the cable for visible damage, kinks, or loose connectors. Why: Loose or damaged connections can produce intermittent or false readings.

steps.title: Inspect Sensor Condition
steps.instructions: Look for wear, frayed wires, or discoloration on reusable sensors. Ensure disposable sensors are not expired. Why: Damaged or expired sensors often fail to read accurately.

steps.title: Verify Proper Sensor Placement on Patient
steps.instructions: Ensure the sensor is applied to a suitable site (finger, toe, or earlobe). Remove nail polish, artificial nails, or excessive moisture if present. Why: Poor placement or optical interference can cause erroneous SpO₂ values.

steps.title: Check for Patient Movement or Perfusion Issues
steps.instructions: Ask the patient to remain still; check for cold extremities or poor perfusion. Use a different site if needed. Why: Motion artifacts or low perfusion can trigger sensor errors or unstable readings.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn the Rad-97 off, wait 10 seconds, then power it back on. Why: Sometimes software resets can clear temporary sensor communication issues.

steps.title: Swap Cables or Sensors if Available
steps.instructions: If another compatible sensor or cable is available, connect it and test. Why: Confirms whether the issue is with the sensor or the oximeter itself.

CCR.Complaint: Rad-97 showing fluctuating SpO₂ readings and sensor error alarms.
CCR.Cause: Sensor improperly seated; cable checked and no visible damage; readings unstable despite repositioning.
CCR.Resolution: Sensor reseated; attempted alternative site and sensor; issue persists—device removed from service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Any unusual readings or alarms displayed

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Touchscreen / Control Panel Problems
description: Guide for troubleshooting touchscreen or control panel issues on the Masimo Rad-97 pulse oximeter.

steps.title: Ensure Device is Powered Correctly
steps.instructions: Confirm the device battery is charged or the power adapter is connected securely. A low battery or intermittent power can cause touchscreen malfunction.

steps.title: Inspect Screen for Debris or Damage
steps.instructions: Clean the touchscreen with a soft, lint-free cloth and approved disinfectant. Check for cracks, scratches, or residue that might interfere with touch sensitivity.

steps.title: Check User Gloves / Protective Covers
steps.instructions: Some medical gloves or screen protectors reduce touchscreen responsiveness. Remove any covers and test touch response.

steps.title: Restart the Device
steps.instructions: Perform a proper power cycle: turn off, wait 10–15 seconds, and turn back on. This can clear temporary software glitches affecting the touchscreen.

steps.title: Verify Software / Settings
steps.instructions: Check that the device is running the latest approved firmware version. Reset display settings to default if the touchscreen remains unresponsive.

steps.title: Inspect External Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure any wired probes or modules are securely attached. Loose connections can sometimes interfere with system responsiveness.

steps.title: Test Basic Input Functions
steps.instructions: Press physical buttons (if available) to confirm that non-touch input works. If physical buttons work but touch does not, the issue is likely localized to the touchscreen.

CCR.Complaint: User reported the Rad-97 touchscreen was unresponsive during patient monitoring.
CCR.Cause: Observed that the touchscreen did not respond to touch inputs; device powered normally and cables were secure; screen was clean and undamaged.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for repair. Patient monitored on alternate device during troubleshooting.

helpfulDetails: Battery level at time of failure
Response of physical buttons if present
Presence of gloves or protective screen covers

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter Pulse Oximeter - Power / Battery Issues
description: Guide for troubleshooting power and battery issues on the Masimo Rad-97 pulse oximeter, focusing on external causes first.

steps.title: Verify Battery Charge and Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure the device is connected to the approved charger. Check that the charging contacts on both the battery and device are clean, free of debris, and aligned. Observe the charging indicator LED: solid or blinking light per Masimo specifications indicates charging status.

steps.title: Test With a Known Good Power Source
steps.instructions: Plug the charger into a verified working outlet. Avoid power strips with switches or surge protectors that might interrupt current.

steps.title: Remove and Reinstall the Battery
steps.instructions: Power down the device if possible. Remove the battery, inspect for corrosion, swelling, or damage. Reinsert securely and attempt to power on.

steps.title: Try a Known Good Battery
steps.instructions: If available, replace the battery with a fully charged, verified working battery. Power on the device.

steps.title: Check for Firmware or Device Alerts
steps.instructions: Some Rad-97 units may display battery or power warnings in the interface. Note any codes or messages for documentation and potential escalation.

CCR.Complaint: Rad-97 would not power on; patient monitoring interrupted.
CCR.Cause: Battery failed to hold charge; charger and power source verified.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, sent to Biomedical Engineering for battery replacement and functional testing.

helpfulDetails: Any unusual noises, smells, or heat from battery
Device behavior when using a replacement battery

title: Masimo Rad-5 Pulse Oximeter - Sensor Not Detected or Low Perfusion Errors
description: Troubleshooting sensor detection failures and low perfusion errors on the Masimo Rad-5 pulse oximeter.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the device from active patient monitoring if readings are unreliable and transfer monitoring to a known working pulse oximeter.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the device and check for sensor not detected messages, low perfusion indicators, or intermittent readings.

steps.title: Check Sensor Connection
steps.instructions: Ensure the connector is fully seated, reconnect firmly, and inspect for bent pins or debris.

steps.title: Inspect Sensor and Cable Condition
steps.instructions: Look for cracked housing, frayed wires, or dirty sensor surfaces and clean if needed.

steps.title: Try a Known Good Sensor
steps.instructions: Swap with a verified working sensor to isolate whether the issue is sensor-related.

steps.title: Check Patient Application and Site
steps.instructions: Ensure proper placement, remove nail polish, warm extremities, and try alternate sites.

steps.title: Assess Environmental and Motion Factors
steps.instructions: Reduce patient movement and shield from bright ambient light.

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Turn the device off, wait 10–15 seconds, and power back on.

CCR.Complaint: Pulse oximeter not detecting sensor and showing low perfusion error.
CCR.Cause: Damaged sensor cable causing intermittent signal loss.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced sensor with known good unit and verified proper operation.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (working or removed from service)

title: Masimo Rad-5 Pulse Oximeter - SpO2 Readings Inaccurate or Unstable
description: Troubleshooting inaccurate or unstable SpO2 readings caused by sensor issues, patient factors, or environmental interference.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If readings are unreliable, do not depend on this device for clinical decisions. Move the patient to a known working monitor.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Observe the device while in use. Check if readings fluctuate rapidly, compare SpO2 with another device, and note alarms or low perfusion indicators.

steps.title: Check Sensor Placement and Condition (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Inspect and reposition the sensor. Ensure proper placement, remove nail polish, confirm alignment, and inspect for damage.

steps.title: Assess Patient Conditions (Perfusion and Motion)
steps.instructions: Check for poor circulation, cold extremities, or excessive movement. Try a different monitoring site if needed.

steps.title: Check Sensor Cable and Connection
steps.instructions: Ensure the sensor cable is fully seated, inspect for bent pins, and swap with a known working sensor if available.

steps.title: Evaluate Ambient Light Interference
steps.instructions: Shield the sensor from bright light and ensure proper closure and fit.

steps.title: Check Device Settings and Mode
steps.instructions: Confirm correct patient mode and ensure no incorrect averaging or sensitivity settings are applied.

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Turn off the unit, remove and reinsert batteries, and power the device back on.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported unstable and fluctuating SpO2 readings on Masimo Rad-5.
CCR.Cause: Damaged and misaligned finger sensor causing poor signal detection.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced sensor with known good unit; verified stable and accurate readings.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (returned to service or sent for repair)

title: Masimo Rad-5 Pulse Oximeter - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Battery not charging or short runtime due to adapter, battery, or connection issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the device from active patient use if battery reliability is in question and use a known working unit instead.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the device and observe for battery indicator not increasing, rapid drain, or unexpected shutdown.

steps.title: Check Power Adapter and Outlet
steps.instructions: Ensure adapter is firmly connected, test outlet with another device, and inspect adapter for damage.

steps.title: Inspect Charging Port and Connections
steps.instructions: Check for debris, bent pins, or looseness and reseat the connector.

steps.title: Check for Charging Indicator Response
steps.instructions: Look for battery icon or LED response and check for intermittent charging by gently moving the connector.

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Turn off device, disconnect power, reseat battery if applicable, reconnect, and restart.

steps.title: Evaluate Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Determine if battery drains quickly, only works plugged in, or fails to hold charge.

steps.title: Test with Known Good Components
steps.instructions: Swap with known good adapter and battery to isolate the faulty component.

CCR.Complaint: Device not charging and shuts off shortly after unplugging.
CCR.Cause: Failed internal battery unable to hold charge after testing with known good adapter.
CCR.Resolution: Removed from service and sent for battery replacement and evaluation.

title: Masimo Rad-5 Pulse Oximeter - Display or Button Failure
description: Troubleshooting unresponsive buttons, blank or dim display, or intermittent screen operation on the Masimo Rad-5 pulse oximeter.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the device from active patient use if the display or controls are not functioning reliably. Use an alternate monitoring device.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the device and confirm the failure. Observe for completely blank screen, dim or flickering display, or buttons not responding or delayed response.

steps.title: Check Battery Status and Power Source
steps.instructions: Replace batteries with new, known-good batteries, ensure correct battery orientation, and power cycle the device.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Examine the screen and keypad area for cracked display, worn or stuck buttons, fluid ingress or residue, and dirt or debris around buttons.

steps.title: Perform a Hard Reset (Power Cycle)
steps.instructions: Remove batteries, wait 30–60 seconds, reinstall batteries, and power on the device.

steps.title: Check Display Visibility Settings and Environment
steps.instructions: Adjust viewing angle, move device to better lighting, and check for faint display indicating backlight failure.

steps.title: Test Button Functionality Individually
steps.instructions: Press each button and observe response for no response, intermittent response, or only certain buttons failing.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported Rad-5 display blank and buttons not responding during spot check.
CCR.Cause: Depleted batteries caused device to power intermittently, affecting display and keypad function.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced batteries, verified normal display and button operation, returned device to service.

helpfulDetails: Presence of physical damage or contamination

title: Masimo Rad-5 Pulse Oximeter - Alarm or Audio Failure
description: Troubleshooting loss of audible alarms or audio issues on the Masimo Rad-5 pulse oximeter.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If alarms are not audible, remove the device from active patient monitoring and transfer the patient to a functioning monitor.

steps.title: Verify Alarm and Audio Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the device and check for no sound during alarms, no keypress tones, low or distorted audio, or intermittent sound.

steps.title: Check Volume Settings (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Access the settings menu, ensure alarm volume is turned up, confirm the device is not muted, and cycle through volume levels.

steps.title: Verify Alarm Limits Are Active
steps.instructions: Ensure SpO2 and pulse rate limits are enabled and trigger a test alarm if safe.

steps.title: Perform a Power Cycle
steps.instructions: Power off the device, remove and reseat batteries if applicable, and restart the device.

steps.title: Inspect Speaker Area
steps.instructions: Inspect the speaker grille for debris, ensure nothing is covering it, and listen for faint output.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage or Liquid Exposure
steps.instructions: Inspect the housing for cracks, impact damage, or fluid ingress and note any corrosion or unusual smells.

steps.title: Test with Known Alarm Condition
steps.instructions: If safe, simulate a low SpO2 or disconnect the sensor briefly to confirm audible alarm function.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported no audible alarms on Rad-5 during patient monitoring.
CCR.Cause: Internal speaker failure confirmed after volume and alarm settings verified functional.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and sent to vendor for repair.

helpfulDetails: Any visible damage or fluid exposure

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Alarm Limits Or Profile Settings Will Not Save
description: Settings that revert or fail to save because of profile restrictions, user permissions, temporary changes, synchronization, software, or configuration storage faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Verify Current Alarm Coverage
steps.instructions: Do not leave a patient connected to a monitor with unverified alarm limits or an incorrect profile. Use another verified monitor or have clinical staff confirm appropriate active limits before Clinical Engineering begins testing. Expected outcome: The patient remains protected by verified alarm settings.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Setting Will Not Save
steps.instructions: Identify the exact alarm limit, profile, display option, or configuration item that changes or reverts. Determine whether it reverts immediately, after leaving the menu, after patient discharge, after profile change, or after restart. Expected outcome: The save failure is reproduced and its timing is documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify User Permissions and Access Level
steps.instructions: Confirm that the person attempting the change has the appropriate authorized access. Do not bypass access controls or use restricted service credentials. Expected outcome: The setting is being changed through an authorized user level.

steps.title: 4. Determine Whether the Change Is Temporary by Design
steps.instructions: Compare the workflow with the approved facility configuration and another Rad-97. Some patient-specific alarm changes may be temporary and may reset when a new patient, profile, or care area is selected. Expected outcome: Expected temporary behavior is distinguished from an actual save failure.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Active Profile
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct profile is selected and that the requested alarm limits are permitted under that profile. Do not modify protected profile parameters without authorization from the responsible clinical and systems owners. Expected outcome: The correct approved profile is active.

steps.title: 6. Save Through the Normal Approved Workflow
steps.instructions: Repeat the change using the complete normal save, confirmation, or profile-selection process. Observe for warning messages or prompts indicating that the change was not accepted. Expected outcome: The setting remains after leaving and reopening the menu. If so, troubleshooting can stop after further verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for Central or Network Configuration Control
steps.instructions: Determine whether a connected central system or configuration-management process automatically applies approved settings. Temporarily evaluate in coordination with the system owner rather than disconnecting or disabling managed configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: A network-managed configuration source is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 8. Restart and Verify Retention
steps.instructions: With the monitor removed from patient use, restart it and confirm whether the authorized saved profile or setting remains. Expected outcome: The approved configuration is retained after restart.

steps.title: 9. Compare With Another Approved Rad-97
steps.instructions: Compare software behavior, profile naming, accessible settings, and retention with a known-good unit in the same department. Do not copy settings informally or alter protected configurations. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to a workflow, profile, network source, or the affected monitor.

steps.title: 10. Verify Alarm Operation
steps.instructions: Use approved test methods to confirm that the displayed alarm limits are active, alarms occur at the expected thresholds, and audible and visual indications function correctly. Expected outcome: The saved settings are operational, not merely displayed.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Configuration Loss
steps.instructions: If authorized settings repeatedly revert or cannot be retained after correct workflow, profile, restart, and network checks, remove the monitor from clinical use. Expected outcome: The device is labeled Out of Service and sent for qualified configuration or repair evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that customized alarm limits returned to previous values after restarting the Rad-97.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that staff were making temporary patient-level changes without saving them to the authorized department profile.
CCR.Resolution: Reviewed the approved profile workflow with department leadership, restored the correct profile, verified limit retention and alarm operation after restart, and returned the device to service.

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Alarm Speaker Or Audible Alarm Failure
description: Missing, weak, distorted, or intermittent audible alarms caused by volume settings, profiles, muted states, obstruction, software, or speaker failure.

steps.title: 1. Remove the Device From Active Patient Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an alarm failure while a patient depends on the Rad-97. Transfer monitoring to another verified device and notify clinical staff that the audible alarm function is unreliable. Expected outcome: The patient remains protected by a verified alarm system.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Audible Alarm Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether all sounds are absent or only specific alarm tones, key sounds, or pulse tones are affected. Observe visual alarm indicators during a controlled alarm condition and note whether the device displays an alarm while remaining silent. Expected outcome: The audible alarm failure is reproduced without relying on patient events.

steps.title: 3. Check Volume and Silence Status
steps.instructions: Verify the active alarm volume, audio pause or silence state, and any visible muted indicators. Confirm that the volume was not reduced by an active profile or authorized configuration. Do not change protected alarm behavior outside facility policy. Expected outcome: Audible alarms sound at the selected level. If normal alarm audio returns, perform final verification and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Correct Patient Profile or Operating Mode
steps.instructions: Compare the active profile and alarm behavior with an approved Rad-97 known to be configured correctly. Confirm that the profile is appropriate for the care area and has not intentionally altered alarm audio behavior. Expected outcome: The approved profile produces expected audible alarms. If corrected, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Speaker Opening and Device Enclosure
steps.instructions: Check the speaker opening for tape, covers, residue, fluid contamination, or mounting hardware that could obstruct sound. Inspect the enclosure for impact damage or evidence of liquid ingress. Do not insert objects into the speaker opening. Expected outcome: The sound path is unobstructed and the enclosure is undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Reboot the Device Safely
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Observe startup tones, self-test indications, and whether audio returns after reboot. Expected outcome: Alarm audio returns and remains reliable. If so, continue to final alarm verification.

steps.title: 7. Test Multiple Audible Functions
steps.instructions: Using approved test methods, check a physiological alarm, technical alarm, alarm-volume adjustment, and any startup or user-interface tones that are normally available. Confirm that visual and audible indications occur together. Expected outcome: All required audible alarm functions operate consistently.

steps.title: 8. Check External Connections and Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories, communication cables, and docking connections that could influence configuration or operation. Retest the alarm speaker in a basic standalone configuration. Expected outcome: Audible alarm operation is restored or the problem remains isolated to the monitor.

steps.title: 9. Perform an Approved Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Use a simulator or controlled method to trigger representative high-priority and technical alarm conditions according to facility procedures. Verify sound level subjectively at the point of use and confirm that no intermittent dropout occurs. Expected outcome: The alarm speaker produces clear, repeatable audible alarms.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Continuing Alarm Failure
steps.instructions: Any device that cannot reliably produce required audible alarms must remain out of service. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 is labeled Out of Service and routed for qualified repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 displayed alarms but produced no audible alarm sound.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the active profile alarm volume set to its lowest authorized level after a profile change.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the approved care-area profile, verified audible and visual alarms using controlled test conditions, and returned the device to service.

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Clock, Time Synchronization, Or Configuration Error
description: Incorrect time or configuration caused by manual settings, profile mismatch, lost synchronization, network problems, power loss, or service-level configuration faults.

steps.title: 1. Assess the Clinical Impact
steps.instructions: Confirm whether incorrect time affects trend review, patient association, network communication, alarm records, or exported data. Do not rely on incorrectly timestamped records for clinical decisions without independent verification. Expected outcome: The effect on patient care and data integrity is understood.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Error
steps.instructions: Record the displayed date, time, time zone, configuration message, and whether the error returns after restart. Compare the Rad-97 with an approved facility time source. Expected outcome: The amount and type of time or configuration error are documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Active Profile
steps.instructions: Confirm that the device is using the approved clinical profile for its department and patient population. Compare it with another authorized Rad-97. Do not alter protected alarm or network settings without approval. Expected outcome: The correct profile is active or an approved profile mismatch is identified.

steps.title: 4. Check Time Zone and Daylight-Saving Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that the configured time zone and daylight-saving behavior match facility policy. Avoid making manual corrections when the device is expected to synchronize automatically unless authorized. Expected outcome: Basic time settings match the facility standard.

steps.title: 5. Verify Network Connection
steps.instructions: If automatic time synchronization is expected, check that the Rad-97 is connected to the approved network and communicating normally. Compare with another device in the same location. Expected outcome: Network connectivity is available for synchronization.

steps.title: 6. Perform an Approved Time Synchronization
steps.instructions: Use the normal authorized synchronization or configuration method supported by the facility. Do not access undocumented service menus or change network security settings. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 displays the correct date and time.

steps.title: 7. Restart and Check Time Retention
steps.instructions: After correcting the time through approved methods, perform a normal restart and verify that the date, time, and profile remain correct. Expected outcome: Settings are retained after restart. If so, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Check AC and Battery History
steps.instructions: Determine whether the unit recently experienced a prolonged power loss, fully depleted battery, battery replacement, or storage period. Verify normal charging and battery operation. Expected outcome: A power-related event explains the lost time or configuration without evidence of continuing failure.

steps.title: 9. Verify Trend and Export Timestamps
steps.instructions: Create a controlled test record and confirm that displayed trends, exported data, and receiving systems show the correct time. Expected outcome: Time is correct throughout the complete data path.

steps.title: 10. Compare Configuration With an Approved Device
steps.instructions: Review only accessible, authorized settings relevant to time and profile configuration. Document any unexplained differences for escalation rather than changing restricted parameters. Expected outcome: The affected device matches the approved configuration.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Recurrent Time or Configuration Loss
steps.instructions: If the Rad-97 loses its clock or settings after restart, power removal, or normal operation, remove it from workflows requiring reliable records or communication. Expected outcome: The device is routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 clock was incorrect and trend records appeared under the wrong time.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the device was assigned an incorrect time zone after being transferred from another department.
CCR.Resolution: Applied the authorized facility time-zone configuration, synchronized the clock, verified time retention and trend timestamps after restart, and returned the device to service.

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Display Blank, Dim, Flickering, Or Frozen
description: Display loss or instability caused by power problems, brightness settings, software lockup, environmental conditions, accessories, or display hardware failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Monitor From Use
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreadable or frozen display while a patient depends on the device. Transfer monitoring to another verified monitor before disconnecting the Rad-97. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without relying on the affected display.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Display Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the display is completely blank, unusually dim, flickering, distorted, delayed, or frozen while values remain unchanged. Observe whether alarm lights, sounds, charging indicators, or network indicators continue to function. Expected outcome: The display symptom is reproduced and separated from a complete power failure.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Battery Operation
steps.instructions: Inspect the approved power supply, cord, plug, and device power connection for damage or looseness. Test the device on a verified outlet and observe behavior on both AC and battery power when safe. Expected outcome: The monitor remains powered and the display is stable on both available power sources. If corrected by reconnecting power, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Display Brightness and Power-Saving Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that the brightness was not reduced, the screen was not intentionally placed in a dimmed state, and the active profile has appropriate display settings. Compare with an approved Rad-97 configuration when available. Expected outcome: Normal brightness returns and remains stable. If so, troubleshooting can stop after final testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Physical or Environmental Causes
steps.instructions: Check the display for cracks, impact damage, fluid intrusion, contamination, or pressure from mounting hardware. Allow the device to reach a normal operating environment if it was exposed to excessive heat, cold, moisture, or condensation. Expected outcome: No external damage or environmental condition explains the problem.

steps.title: 6. Disconnect Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Remove USB devices, external communication cables, and other nonessential accessories. Restart the monitor in a basic standalone configuration. Expected outcome: The display operates normally without external accessories. If one accessory causes the fault, remove that accessory from use.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With the device out of clinical use, complete a normal shutdown and restart. Observe the startup sequence, logo, indicators, touch response, and whether the screen freezes again. Expected outcome: The device boots normally and the display remains responsive. If stable, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Check Touch and Control Response
steps.instructions: Verify that the screen and physical controls respond consistently and that displayed values update normally. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or alter protected configurations. Expected outcome: Displayed information updates and controls respond without delay or freezing.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional and Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Connect approved test accessories and confirm that saturation, pulse rate, pleth waveform, menu navigation, visual alarms, and audible alarms display correctly. Operate the device long enough to confirm that flickering or freezing does not return. Expected outcome: The display remains clear, stable, and responsive throughout testing.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Display Failure
steps.instructions: A monitor with an unreadable, flickering, or intermittently frozen display is not reliable for clinical use. Expected outcome: The device is removed from service and sent for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 display became dim and intermittently flickered during use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose connection at the external power supply that caused unstable operation while the battery was nearly depleted.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the approved power connection, charged the unit, confirmed stable display operation on AC and battery power, verified monitoring and alarms, and returned it to service.

helpfulDetails: Blank, dim, flickering, distorted, or frozen condition

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Low Perfusion Causes Persistent No-Read Condition
description: Persistent no-read conditions associated with weak peripheral perfusion, poor sensor placement, motion, cable problems, or unsuitable measurement sites.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unreliable monitoring equipment while a patient depends on it. Transfer the patient to another verified pulse oximeter or use an appropriate alternate monitoring method before removing or repositioning the sensor. Confirm that clinical staff are assessing the patient independently and not relying on an absent saturation reading. Expected outcome: Continuous patient monitoring is maintained while the Rad-97 is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Ask whether the no-read condition occurs continuously or intermittently, on one patient or multiple patients, and at a specific site or under particular conditions such as cold extremities, hypotension, movement, transport, or vasoconstriction. Observe the displayed indicators, messages, Signal IQ information, and pleth behavior without changing clinical settings unnecessarily. Expected outcome: The failure is confirmed and distinguished from an isolated patient-specific low-perfusion event.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Measurement Site
steps.instructions: Check whether the selected site is cold, poorly perfused, compressed, edematous, injured, positioned below a blood pressure cuff, or affected by excessive motion. Have clinical staff select another clinically appropriate, better-perfused site when permitted. Expected outcome: A stable pleth waveform and numerical reading appear after correcting the measurement site. If readings remain stable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Sensor Placement and Alignment
steps.instructions: Inspect the sensor for correct positioning, full contact, proper emitter-to-detector alignment, and secure application without excessive pressure. Confirm that reusable sensors are clean and that disposable sensors are not loose, folded, contaminated, or repeatedly reapplied beyond their intended condition. Expected outcome: The sensor detects pulsatile flow and produces a consistent reading. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Reduce Motion and Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Stabilize the monitored extremity and cable. Check for tremor, shivering, patient movement, transport vibration, or cable tugging. Shield the sensor from intense direct light when appropriate and verify that no external source is interfering with the optical path. Expected outcome: Signal quality improves and the no-read condition clears. If stable readings are restored, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Sensor, Patient Cable, and Connections
steps.instructions: Examine the sensor, patient cable, adapter, and monitor connector for contamination, bent contacts, damaged insulation, strain, looseness, or incomplete insertion. Disconnect and reconnect each accessible connection securely. Do not force connectors. Expected outcome: All connections remain secure and the signal returns without manipulation. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Test the monitor using a compatible known-good sensor and patient cable approved for the Rad-97. Test the suspect sensor and cable on another compatible verified monitor when available. Expected outcome: The substitution identifies whether the problem follows the sensor, cable, or monitor. Replace the failed external accessory and stop if normal performance is restored.

steps.title: 8. Compare Performance on a Suitable Test Subject or Simulator
steps.instructions: After removing the device from patient use, test it on a suitable staff test subject or approved pulse oximetry simulator according to facility procedures. Do not use a simulator result alone to dismiss a genuine patient perfusion concern. Expected outcome: The monitor acquires and maintains a stable signal under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify stable saturation, pulse rate, pleth waveform, signal quality indication, sensor-off response, and applicable alarms using approved test methods. Confirm that the device functions without cable manipulation or intermittent signal loss. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 performs consistently and is suitable for return to service.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved No-Read Condition
steps.instructions: If the Rad-97 repeatedly fails to acquire a signal with compatible known-good sensors, cables, suitable sites, and controlled testing, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The device is removed from clinical use and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 remained in a no-read condition on a patient with weak peripheral perfusion.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found poor sensor contact at a cold, poorly perfused finger and verified that the monitor operated normally with a known-good sensor at an alternate site.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the sensor at a suitable site, confirmed a stable pleth waveform and numerical readings, tested alarm response, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact displayed message or status indicator

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Patient Cable Or Adapter Intermittent
description: Intermittent sensor detection or readings caused by loose connections, damaged cables, worn adapters, strain, contamination, or monitor connector problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Replace Unreliable Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an intermittent monitoring cable while a patient depends on it. Transfer the patient to another verified monitor or replace the affected monitoring path immediately. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without intermittent signal loss.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Intermittent Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the signal drops during movement, cable flexing, bed adjustment, transport, or repositioning. Observe messages, pleth waveform, Signal IQ, sensor status, and numerical readings without deliberately stressing the cable while it is connected to a patient. Expected outcome: The reported intermittent failure is confirmed and associated with a specific condition.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Sensor Connection
steps.instructions: Check that the sensor is fully seated in the patient cable or adapter and that locking features engage correctly. Inspect for contamination, moisture, bent contacts, worn fit, or damage. Expected outcome: The sensor connection remains secure and readings stabilize. If successful, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Patient Cable and Adapter
steps.instructions: Examine the full cable length, strain reliefs, connectors, and adapter housing for cuts, kinks, crushing, discoloration, exposed conductors, or prior repairs. Remove any damaged cable or adapter from service. Expected outcome: Only intact external accessories remain in use.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Rad-97 Connector
steps.instructions: Check the monitor connector for contamination, looseness, damaged contacts, or evidence that the plug does not remain fully seated. Do not probe or reshape contacts. Expected outcome: The monitor connector is clean, undamaged, and holds the cable securely.

steps.title: 6. Reconnect and Route the Cable Correctly
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the cable without force. Route it to avoid tension, sharp bends, snagging, bed mechanisms, wheels, and patient movement. Expected outcome: The signal remains stable during normal repositioning.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Patient Cable and Adapter
steps.instructions: Use compatible approved known-good accessories while keeping the same monitor and sensor. Expected outcome: The intermittent condition disappears, identifying the original cable or adapter as defective. Replace it and stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Test the Suspect Accessory on Another Compatible Monitor
steps.instructions: When appropriate, test the suspect cable or adapter on another verified compatible device under controlled conditions. Expected outcome: The problem follows the accessory or remains with the original Rad-97.

steps.title: 9. Test With a Known-Good Sensor
steps.instructions: Use a compatible known-good sensor to ensure that an intermittent sensor lead is not being mistaken for a cable or adapter problem. Expected outcome: The signal remains stable or the sensor is identified as the cause.

steps.title: 10. Perform Controlled Movement Testing
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, use an approved simulator or suitable test method and gently reposition the cable through normal expected movement. Do not apply excessive bending or destructive stress. Expected outcome: No signal dropout, sensor disconnect, or waveform interruption occurs.

steps.title: 11. Complete Functional and Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm stable readings, pleth waveform, Signal IQ, sensor disconnect alarm, and recovery after reconnection. Expected outcome: The monitoring path is reliable and suitable for return to service.

steps.title: 12. Escalate a Suspected Monitor Connector Failure
steps.instructions: If the problem remains with multiple known-good sensors, cables, and adapters, remove the Rad-97 from service. Expected outcome: The monitor is labeled Out of Service and routed for connector or internal input evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 repeatedly lost the pulse oximetry signal when the patient cable was moved.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an intermittent open condition near the patient cable strain relief, confirmed by substitution with a known-good cable.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged patient cable, verified stable readings during controlled movement, tested sensor-disconnect alarms, and returned the device to service.

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Signal IQ Poor Or Pleth Waveform Missing
description: Poor signal quality or absent pleth waveform caused by motion, placement, perfusion, sensor damage, cable problems, or display configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not continue using unreliable monitoring while a patient depends on it. Move the patient to another verified monitor or establish an appropriate alternate monitoring method before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring remains continuous during evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Signal Problem
steps.instructions: Observe whether Signal IQ is consistently poor, the pleth waveform is missing, or both conditions occur together. Determine whether numerical values are present, unstable, delayed, or absent. Confirm whether the issue affects one patient, one sensor, or every setup. Expected outcome: The reported condition is reproduced and clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Check the Sensor Site and Perfusion
steps.instructions: Inspect the site for cold skin, low perfusion, edema, excessive pressure, nail coverings, poor contact, or placement on an extremity affected by a blood pressure cuff. Use a clinically appropriate alternate site when authorized. Expected outcome: Signal IQ improves and a stable pleth waveform appears. If it remains stable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Correct Sensor Placement
steps.instructions: Verify that the sensor is properly aligned, fully seated, and secure without being overly tight. Ensure the optical components face each other correctly and are not obstructed by contamination, adhesive folds, or damaged material. Expected outcome: A consistent waveform and signal quality indication are restored. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Minimize Motion and Cable Strain
steps.instructions: Stabilize the extremity and route the patient cable to prevent pulling, swinging, or repeated movement at the sensor. Check for tremor, shivering, transport vibration, or nearby equipment contacting the cable. Expected outcome: Signal quality becomes stable when motion and cable strain are reduced.

steps.title: 6. Check Display and Waveform Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify that the pleth waveform is enabled and visible in the active display layout or profile. Do not change clinical alarm limits or protected configuration settings without authorization. Compare the display with another Rad-97 using the same approved profile when available. Expected outcome: The waveform is visible when enabled and configured correctly. If this resolves the issue, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Inspect All External Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect the sensor, patient cable, adapter, and monitor connection for damage, contamination, bent contacts, loose fit, or worn strain relief. Reconnect all accessible connections securely. Expected outcome: The signal remains stable without moving or holding the cable.

steps.title: 8. Test With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Substitute a compatible known-good sensor and patient cable. Test the suspect accessories on another verified compatible device when appropriate. Expected outcome: The problem follows a failed accessory or remains with the Rad-97. Replace the defective external accessory if identified.

steps.title: 9. Test Under Controlled Conditions
steps.instructions: Remove the device from patient care and test it with an approved simulator or suitable controlled test subject. Observe Signal IQ, pleth waveform, pulse rate, saturation response, and stability. Expected outcome: The device produces a stable waveform and normal signal indication under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 10. Complete Functional Verification or Escalate
steps.instructions: Verify waveform display, sensor detection, alarm response, and stable operation after correction. If poor Signal IQ or a missing waveform continues with known-good accessories and controlled testing, remove the unit from service. Expected outcome: The device either passes final verification or is routed for bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported poor Signal IQ and no visible pleth waveform during pulse oximetry monitoring.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged patient cable that produced an unstable signal when flexed near the connector.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the patient cable with a compatible approved cable, confirmed stable Signal IQ and pleth waveform, verified alarms, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Final alarm and functional test results

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Software Freeze, Boot Loop, Or Startup Failure
description: Startup or software failures caused by unstable power, depleted battery, attached accessories, corrupted configuration, incomplete updates, or internal system faults.

steps.title: 1. Remove the Device From Patient Use
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a frozen, restarting, or non-starting monitor while a patient depends on it. Transfer monitoring to another verified device immediately. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues on reliable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the Rad-97 freezes during operation, remains on a startup screen, repeatedly restarts, shuts down during boot, or does not progress beyond initial indicators. Record the last visible screen, message, tone, and indicator behavior. Expected outcome: The failure stage is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Damage, Heat, Odor, or Fluid Intrusion
steps.instructions: Check the enclosure, vents, connectors, power supply, and battery area for impact damage, abnormal heat, odor, swelling, residue, or fluid exposure. Do not power the device again if unsafe physical conditions are present. Expected outcome: The device is either safe for limited external testing or immediately removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the External Power Source
steps.instructions: Inspect the approved power supply and connections. Test on a verified outlet and confirm that the power connector remains secure. Avoid repeated power cycling if the device becomes hot or emits unusual sounds or odor. Expected outcome: Stable external power is available and the device begins a normal startup.

steps.title: 5. Allow Battery Charging
steps.instructions: If the battery is deeply depleted, connect the approved power supply and allow sufficient charging according to facility and manufacturer guidance before retesting. Expected outcome: The monitor starts normally after adequate charging. If stable, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Disconnect Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Remove sensors, patient cables, USB devices, network cables, adapters, and other nonessential external accessories. Attempt startup with only approved power connected. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 starts normally in a basic configuration. Reconnect accessories individually to identify an external cause.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Use the normal power control and shutdown process when responsive. Do not repeatedly interrupt startup or use undocumented reset methods. Expected outcome: The monitor completes startup and remains responsive.

steps.title: 8. Observe Startup Self-Checks
steps.instructions: Watch for consistent progress through the startup sequence, normal display operation, audible indications, and absence of repeated rebooting. Expected outcome: Startup completes without errors or looping.

steps.title: 9. Verify Configuration and Software History
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem began after an authorized software update, profile change, network change, or accessory connection. Do not reinstall software, downgrade versions, or access restricted service functions without approved procedures. Expected outcome: A recent authorized change is identified for escalation or rollback by qualified personnel.

steps.title: 10. Perform Extended Functional Testing
steps.instructions: After successful startup, verify display, controls, sensor detection, pleth waveform, numerical readings, alarms, charging, battery operation, network status, and stability over time. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 remains stable through repeated normal operation.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Recurring Software or Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Any device that repeats a boot loop, freezes again, or cannot complete startup must remain out of service. Expected outcome: The unit is labeled Out of Service and sent for qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 repeatedly restarted and would not progress beyond the startup screen.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an unapproved USB device connected to the monitor and verified that startup completed normally after it was removed.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the unapproved accessory, completed repeated startup and extended functional testing, verified monitoring and alarms, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Last visible startup screen or message
Physical damage, heat, odor, or fluid exposure

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Trend Memory Full Or Stored Data Retrieval Failure
description: Trend storage or retrieval problems caused by full memory, filters, patient selection, date settings, software state, export issues, or internal storage faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Active Patient Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt current monitoring solely to investigate stored data. Confirm that current values and alarms remain functional. Use another verified monitor if the Rad-97 is freezing, restarting, or otherwise affecting active care. Expected outcome: Current patient monitoring remains uninterrupted.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Data Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the device reports full memory, cannot save new trends, cannot display stored records, shows missing time periods, or fails only during export. Record the displayed message and the data range clinical staff expected to retrieve. Expected outcome: The storage or retrieval failure is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Correct Patient and Date Selection
steps.instructions: Check that the correct patient record, date range, trend type, and display filter are selected. Review the device date and time for obvious errors that could place records under an unexpected timestamp. Expected outcome: The expected data becomes visible after correcting selection or time-range filters. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Current Storage Status
steps.instructions: Review available storage indicators using normal operator-accessible menus. Do not delete records without authorization and facility policy. Confirm whether required data has already been transferred or retained elsewhere before any approved clearing action. Expected outcome: The storage condition is identified without losing required clinical information.

steps.title: 5. Confirm the Device Is Saving New Data
steps.instructions: Create a controlled test record using approved methods and verify whether new trend data appears with the correct timestamp. Expected outcome: New data is saved and retrieved normally, indicating the issue may be limited to older records or filtering.

steps.title: 6. Restart the Device Safely
steps.instructions: Transfer active monitoring to another device and perform a normal shutdown and restart. Recheck stored data and available memory after startup. Expected outcome: Data retrieval resumes and the device remains stable. If successful, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Export Media or Connected Systems
steps.instructions: If retrieval fails only during export, inspect the approved USB device, cable, external system, or communication path. Test with a known-good compatible export device according to facility policy. Expected outcome: Stored data exports successfully or the problem is isolated to external media or communication.

steps.title: 8. Compare With an Approved Rad-97
steps.instructions: Compare normal data menu behavior, filters, profile, time settings, and storage workflow with another approved Rad-97. Do not copy or change protected settings without authorization. Expected outcome: A configuration or workflow difference is identified and corrected through approved methods.

steps.title: 9. Preserve Required Data Before Clearing Memory
steps.instructions: If memory is confirmed full, coordinate with clinical leadership, health information management, or the responsible system owner before deleting or clearing data. Follow approved facility and manufacturer procedures only. Expected outcome: Required data is retained and storage is restored without unauthorized deletion.

steps.title: 10. Verify Storage and Retrieval
steps.instructions: Create, save, retrieve, and, when required, export a new controlled test record. Confirm correct date, time, patient association, and trend display. Expected outcome: Trend storage and retrieval operate normally.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Storage Failure
steps.instructions: If the Rad-97 cannot reliably save or retrieve data after approved memory, filter, time, restart, and export checks, remove it from workflows that require trend storage. Expected outcome: The device is routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that recent Rad-97 trend data could not be found and the device indicated that storage was full.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that older retained records had filled available trend storage and confirmed the expected recent record was listed under an incorrect date range.
CCR.Resolution: Preserved required records, completed an authorized memory-clearing process, corrected the date range selection, verified new trend storage and retrieval, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Final save, retrieve, and export verification

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Unexpected Shutdown During Battery Operation
description: Unexpected battery shutdown caused by incomplete charging, aged battery capacity, loose power connections, high load, temperature, software, or internal power faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Restore Continuous Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not continue using a monitor that shuts down unexpectedly while a patient depends on it. Transfer monitoring to another verified device and connect the Rad-97 to approved AC power only after it is removed from the patient. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without risk of another shutdown.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Shutdown Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine the displayed battery level before shutdown, estimated operating time, whether alarms occurred, and whether the device restarted when AC power was connected. Ask whether the shutdown occurs every time on battery or only during transport, movement, or use of attached accessories. Expected outcome: The shutdown condition is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Battery Safety Concerns
steps.instructions: Check for enclosure swelling, excessive heat, odor, leakage, discoloration, or physical damage. If any battery safety concern is present, do not charge or operate the device. Remove it from service and follow facility battery-handling procedures. Expected outcome: The unit is safe for controlled testing or isolated immediately.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Approved Power Supply and Outlet
steps.instructions: Inspect the power supply, cord, plug, and device connector. Connect to a verified outlet and confirm charging indications. Ensure the connector remains secure and is not intermittently losing AC power. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 recognizes AC power and begins charging normally.

steps.title: 5. Allow a Complete Approved Charge
steps.instructions: Charge the device according to facility and manufacturer guidance before testing runtime. Do not judge battery condition from a brief charge period. Expected outcome: The battery indicator shows a completed or normal charge state.

steps.title: 6. Check Battery Indicator Behavior
steps.instructions: Disconnect AC power under controlled bench conditions and observe whether the battery indicator decreases normally or falls abruptly. Expected outcome: Battery status changes gradually and the device remains operating.

steps.title: 7. Remove Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect USB devices, external communication accessories, and other nonessential loads. Repeat battery operation testing with only required monitoring accessories. Expected outcome: The device remains powered, or an attached accessory is identified as contributing to abnormal shutdown.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Power Connector During Movement
steps.instructions: With the device on AC power, gently reposition the external cord through normal movement and observe for power-source switching or charging interruptions. Do not stress the connector. Expected outcome: AC power and charging remain stable without interruption.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Battery Runtime Test
steps.instructions: Using approved facility procedures and test conditions, operate the fully charged Rad-97 on battery while monitoring battery indication, alarms, temperature, and shutdown behavior. Do not place the device into clinical service solely to test runtime. Expected outcome: The monitor operates reliably for the facility’s accepted test requirement without abrupt shutdown.

steps.title: 10. Verify Low-Battery Alarm and Shutdown Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that low-battery warnings occur before shutdown and that the device does not lose power without adequate warning. Expected outcome: Battery alarms and shutdown behavior are orderly and repeatable.

steps.title: 11. Recheck After Battery Replacement When Authorized
steps.instructions: If testing confirms inadequate battery capacity and battery replacement is permitted under approved procedures, install the correct approved battery through qualified service. Do not improvise battery substitutions. Expected outcome: The monitor charges normally and passes controlled battery testing.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final Functional Verification or Escalate
steps.instructions: Verify operation on AC and battery, charging, battery indication, low-battery alarms, monitoring, display, network communication where applicable, and all audible and visual alarms. If unexpected shutdown persists, remove the device from service. Expected outcome: The device passes complete verification or is routed for qualified repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 shut down unexpectedly during patient transport even though the battery indicator initially showed available charge.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the battery voltage indication dropped abruptly under load and the unit failed the facility’s controlled battery runtime test.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the approved battery through the authorized service process, verified charging, runtime, low-battery alarms, monitoring, and alarm operation, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Final charging, alarm, and device status

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - USB Export Or External Device Communication Failure
description: USB export or external communication problems caused by media compatibility, cables, connectors, permissions, data format, configuration, or interface failure.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Patient Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt active monitoring to troubleshoot data export. Confirm that local monitoring and alarms remain normal. Transfer the patient to another verified monitor if the Rad-97 freezes, restarts, or becomes unreliable when an external device is connected. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring remains safe and uninterrupted.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the Rad-97 fails to recognize the USB device, cannot begin export, stops partway through, creates an unreadable file, or cannot communicate with a connected external system. Record all displayed messages and the type of external device involved. Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced and clearly categorized.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the USB Device, Cable, and Connector
steps.instructions: Check the external device, cable, adapter, and Rad-97 port for damage, contamination, looseness, bent contacts, or evidence of fluid exposure. Do not force a connector or use unapproved adapters. Expected outcome: All external components are intact and fully connected.

steps.title: 4. Verify Approved Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the media, cable, adapter, or external device is approved and compatible with the facility’s Rad-97 configuration. Do not connect personal storage devices or unapproved equipment to a clinical device. Expected outcome: Only approved compatible accessories remain connected.

steps.title: 5. Test With a Known-Good External Device
steps.instructions: Use a known-good approved USB device, cable, or connected system. Test the suspect accessory on another verified compatible device when permitted. Expected outcome: The problem follows the external accessory or remains with the Rad-97.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Data Selection and Available Storage
steps.instructions: Verify that valid data is selected for export and that the external storage device has sufficient available space. Confirm that the expected export process is being used and that no required selection field is missing. Expected outcome: The export begins and completes normally. If so, troubleshooting can stop after file verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Date, Time, and File Identification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the Rad-97 date and time are correct so exported files can be found and associated properly. Review the destination for a newly created file rather than relying only on the expected filename. Expected outcome: The exported record is located with the correct timestamp.

steps.title: 8. Disconnect Other Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Remove additional external devices and communication cables, then retry using only the required known-good connection. Expected outcome: Export or communication succeeds without accessory conflict.

steps.title: 9. Restart and Retest
steps.instructions: Remove the unit from patient use, perform a normal restart, and retry the export or external communication process. Expected outcome: The Rad-97 recognizes the external device and completes the process reliably.

steps.title: 10. Verify the Exported Data or External Communication
steps.instructions: Open the exported file on an approved secure workstation or verify data reception at the intended external system. Confirm completeness, correct patient association, date, time, and readability. Expected outcome: The full data transfer is verified end to end.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If the problem remains with multiple approved known-good accessories, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The monitor is removed from workflows requiring USB or external communication and routed for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 would not recognize a USB device during trend export.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the USB device was not approved for the monitor and verified normal operation with a compatible hospital-controlled device.
CCR.Resolution: Repeated the export using an approved USB device, confirmed the complete file on a secure workstation, verified normal monitoring and alarms, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Type of USB or external device

title: Masimo Rad-97 Pulse Oximeter - Wi-Fi Or Network Communication Failure
description: Loss of wireless or network communication caused by signal coverage, incorrect profiles, access restrictions, infrastructure, time settings, or interface configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Clarify Monitoring Dependence
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the Rad-97 is being used for local monitoring only or whether clinicians depend on central alarm or data communication. If remote alarm visibility is required and communication is unavailable, provide another verified monitoring path before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient has a confirmed local and remote monitoring method as required.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the device cannot connect to Wi-Fi, connects without transmitting data, drops connection intermittently, or communicates in some rooms but not others. Record visible network icons, messages, and the affected destination system. Expected outcome: The communication problem is accurately defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Monitoring Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the Rad-97 continues to measure, display, and alarm locally. A network problem must not be confused with a complete monitor malfunction. Expected outcome: Local monitoring is either verified or the device is removed from service for a broader failure.

steps.title: 4. Check Location and Wireless Coverage
steps.instructions: Move the device within the approved clinical area and compare network status with another known-good Rad-97 or approved wireless device. Check whether the issue occurs near known coverage gaps, elevators, shielded rooms, or recently changed infrastructure. Expected outcome: Communication returns in an area with verified coverage, indicating an infrastructure or location-related problem.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Network Profile
steps.instructions: Confirm that the active network, clinical profile, and destination configuration match an approved Rad-97 in the same department. Do not enter credentials, change security settings, or modify protected network configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The device is using the approved network configuration.

steps.title: 6. Check Date and Time
steps.instructions: Verify that the device date, time, and time zone are reasonable and aligned with facility systems. Incorrect time may interfere with secure communication, data association, or event display. Expected outcome: Time settings are correct or synchronized through the approved method.

steps.title: 7. Restart the Device and Recheck Connection
steps.instructions: With monitoring transferred to another device, perform a normal restart. Observe whether the Rad-97 reconnects automatically and resumes data communication. Expected outcome: The network connection restores and remains stable. If communication is verified end to end, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Inspect External Network Connections
steps.instructions: For any wired interface, inspect the cable, connector, wall port, adapter, or docking interface for damage, looseness, or incorrect connection. Test with a known-good approved cable and verified active port when available. Expected outcome: The device communicates through the verified connection.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Complete Data Path
steps.instructions: Confirm that the receiving system identifies the correct device and patient context, receives current values, and displays alarms or data as intended. Coordinate with clinical systems, networking, or interface teams when the Rad-97 is connected but data does not reach the destination. Expected outcome: Current data is visible at the intended receiving system.

steps.title: 10. Isolate Device Versus Infrastructure Failure
steps.instructions: Test another known-good Rad-97 in the same location and the affected Rad-97 in a known-good location. Expected outcome: The comparison identifies whether the problem follows the monitor or remains with the room, network, or interface.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Communication Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm local monitoring, network status, correct device identity, current data transmission, alarm path where applicable, and stable communication after movement or restart. Expected outcome: The complete communication path operates reliably.

steps.title: 12. Escalate an Unresolved Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If the problem follows the Rad-97 after approved profile, time, coverage, cable, and port checks, remove it from the affected workflow. Expected outcome: The unit is labeled Out of Service for network use and routed for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Rad-97 monitored locally but no data appeared at the receiving station.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the monitor connected to an incorrect approved wireless profile after being moved from another department.
CCR.Resolution: Applied the authorized department profile, confirmed stable Wi-Fi connection and current data at the receiving station, verified local alarms, and returned the device to service.
